The Constraints That a Break-Point on an Observation Places

Source: R/segmented.R
term_kink_constraints.SegTerm.Rd

Returns, for each break-point of a sharp seg() that sits on an observation at the given coefficients, the row of the linear constraint that keeps it there. The row is the unit vector of its position where the position is not developed, and the development's row \(z_j\) at the position's coefficients where it is, so that the kink lies on the hyperplane \(z_j^\top\kappa = x_j\).

Arguments

term

A built seg() term.

coef

The term's coefficients. NULL reads the stored ones.

...

Unused.

Value

A numeric matrix with one column per coefficient of the term and one row per distinct constraint. If no break-point sits on an observation, the matrix has no rows. A smoothed seg() has no rows.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = runif(60, 0, 10), w = runif(60))
b <- term_build(seg(x, psi ~ w), d)
ix <- b@blueprint$index$psi1
cf <- b@blueprint$coef
# the break-point of the first observation is placed on that observation
cf[ix[1L]] <- d$x[1L] - cf[ix[2L]] * d$w[1L]
term_kink_constraints(b, cf)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]      [,4]
#> [1,]    0    0    1 0.9128759
